messages:
maria: Quick heads-up: canary is showing intermittent SSE pauses (~6s) where client reconnects with resume token and we end up charging a full generation on resume. Billing docs now show duplicate charges for some tenants.

raj: Is the proxy returning a close or a 204 during the pause?

maria: Proxy logs show a `204` midstream. Client still had resume_token and immediately rejoined. Billing pipeline treats the rejoin as a fresh generation.

jordan: Console traces show resume_count and new_generation_count both incrementing for the same original_request_id. Looks like the resume path isn't tagged properly for billing.

sam: Can we reproduce with the proxy dev flag enabled?

maria: Yes, repro in staging with PROXY_SIMULATE_MIDSTREAM_204=true. Steps: curl with Resume-Token, then simulate upstream pause ~6s. Client reconnects with same token; server logs mark as resume but billing emits new_generation event.

raj: Hypotheses: (1) proxy strips `x-resume-id` or `x-route-affinity` on 204 path; (2) billing middleware runs a separate auth/namespace lookup losing original_request_id; (3) quota router recalculates route_key when header missing and treats it as new.

jordan: Telemetry: we bucket by session_id+route_key. We observed route_key flips for affected streams. That would explain console and billing deltas.

maria: Short-term mitigation proposal: debounce billing generation events on resume for 10s and check original_request_id to make resume idempotent.

sam: Debounce risks hiding true double-charges. Prefer patching proxy to preserve headers.

raj: Agreed. Immediate action: add a console trace flag to mark "resume vs reconnect" in per-request traces so SREs can triage without changing prod billing. Long-term: patch proxy to keep `x-resume-id` and `x-route-affinity` across 204/hold states.

jordan: Also UX change: rollout banner says "streaming canary: healthy" today, but resume churn increased. Propose adding a streaming health metric (resume_rate vs successful_resume_rate) into rollout scoring.

maria: +1. Also request a console graph for "duplicate_token_generation_events" per tenant so customers can spot billing blips.

ops-bot: [alert] 1718842300 - reconnect spike on canary: tenant=acme-co +320% in 5m

sam: I'll push a small proxy build to preserve headers on midstream 204 and enable the dev flag on canary only.

maria: Patch branch `fix/proxy-preserve-resume-headers` and canary build `canary-2026-03-22-17` created.

raj: Test plan: 1) reproduce pause with and without proxy patch; 2) verify `x-resume-id` preserved in upstream logs; 3) check console traces for route_key flips; 4) confirm billing emits resume_count increment without new_generation increment.

jordan: I'll add a temporary telemetry tile to canary dashboard: `resume_vs_new_gen` and alert if deviation > 5%.

maria: Initial canary looks promising: header preserved, no route_key flips, billing didn't emit extra generations in my quick checks.

sam: Deploy started for canary-2026-03-22-17 by sam at 1718842355

sam: Monitoring live. Ping if you see regressions. :eyes: 

maria: Filing follow-up: if edge cases persist we'll consider limited debounce in billing pipeline as defense-in-depth.

deploy-bot: Deploy success for canary-2026-03-22-17 at 1718842460

raj: Marking for postmortem if promoted. Add playbook note to verify resume headers during canary rollouts.

maria: TL;DR: root cause = proxy dropping route-affinity header during midstream 204; fix deployed to canary; added console telemetry tile; follow-up PM to assess billing debounce as fallback. :thumbsup:
